name: Fish Audio
positioning: Fish Audio is a voice platform and developer API offering expressive text-to-speech (S2.1-Pro) with voice cloning, a community voice library, and OpenAI/ElevenLabs-compatible routes.

pricing.model: Pay-as-you-go API billed per million UTF-8 bytes of input text, with no subscription or monthly minimum for API access; concurrency limits rise with total prepaid amount.
pricing.headline: $15.00 per 1M UTF-8 bytes for the s2.1-pro model (equal to about 1M characters of plain English/ASCII text); s2.1-pro-free is listed at $0 under a fair-use policy.

tiers.name: s2.1-pro
tiers.notes: Recommended production model; TTFA and DPA commitments apply to this model per the models page. Priced per million UTF-8 bytes; one byte is one character for ASCII text, so the figure is exact for plain English and higher per character for scripts that use multi-byte UTF-8 (a derived reading of the unit).

tiers.name: s2-pro
tiers.notes: Previous-generation S2 model, same listed price.

tiers.name: s1 (deprecated)
tiers.notes: Retiring December 31, 2026; requests naming s1 are then served and billed as s2.1-pro at the same price.

tiers.name: s2.1-pro-free
tiers.notes: Same model as s2.1-pro for development and testing; fair-use limits, no TTFA or DPA commitments, no hard character cap stated.

tiers.name: Speech-to-text (transcribe-1 / transcribe-1-pro)
tiers.notes: Not a text-to-speech price; recorded for completeness.

tiers.name: Voice Design (voice-design-1)
tiers.notes: Covers one request even when it returns several candidate voices.

pricing.freeTier: Model string s2.1-pro-free at $0 under a fair-use policy; per the vendor blog it has no SLA or latency commitment, requests may be used to improve model quality, and products above $1M ARR are asked to contact Fish Audio first.
promotions: Free access to s2.1-pro-free: the vendor blog shows several superseded end dates and its latest statement reads 'Free access is available through November 30, 2026'. Treat the end date as subject to change; the blog says changes will be communicated with notice.

voices.count: 2,000,000+ voices on the platform (vendor homepage; includes user-uploaded community voices)
voices.languages: 83 languages for s2.1-pro (80+ for s2-pro), with automatic language detection
voices.customVoiceOrCloning: Voice cloning from reference audio via API and web app; homepage says as little as 10 seconds of audio is needed; voice cloning is also available on the free model per the vendor blog.

streaming.vendorStatedLatency: Vendor-stated: docs say latency=balanced (default) gives time-to-first-audio of about 300 ms; the models page lists 100 ms TTFA for s2-pro; the vendor blog cites about 90 ms (and elsewhere about 70 ms) TTFA for s2.1-pro. These are vendor figures from different pages and were not measured here.

compatibility.note: Vendor migration guide lists an OpenAI-SDK base URL https://api.fish.audio/compat/v1 (POST /audio/speech), plus OpenRouter-, ElevenLabs- (https://api.fish.audio/compat/elevenlabs) and Groq-style bases. Differences noted by the vendor: voice is a Fish voice ID, response_format defaults to pcm, instructions and stream_format=sse are refused with a 400. Names tts-1, tts-1-hd and gpt-4o-mini-tts are accepted as aliases of fish-audio/s2.1-pro.

licensing.commercialUse: Terms of Service: users of Paid Services are licensed to use the Services for commercial uses; the free web plan is for personal use (homepage FAQ). s2.1-pro-free: the vendor blog says some commercial scenarios may have restrictions and asks products above $1M ARR to contact Fish Audio.
licensing.attributionOrConditions: No attribution requirement for paid use found on the pages read; free-model fair-use and ARR condition as above.

limits.concurrency: Concurrent requests by prepaid total: Starter (under $100 paid) 5; Elevated ($100 or more) 15; High Volume ($1,000 or more) 50; Enterprise custom. Over the limit the native API returns 429.

compliance.note: No HIPAA, SOC 2 or GDPR compliance statement was found on the documentation, pricing or terms pages read; the privacy policy exists but was not treated as a compliance claim.

strengths.claim: Provides OpenAI-, OpenRouter-, ElevenLabs- and Groq-style compatibility bases so existing SDK code can be pointed at Fish Audio.
s2.1-pro supports 83 languages with automatic language detection and natural-language bracket tags for emotion and delivery, such as [whispers sweetly].
Offers a free development model (s2.1-pro-free) with the same quality and language coverage as the paid model, plus a very large community voice library and cloning from short reference audio.
Publishes simple pay-as-you-go pricing with no subscription fee or monthly minimum for API access.
Offers both HTTP streaming and WebSocket streaming for LLM-to-speech use, plus a voice-agent product and speech-to-text.

limitations.claim: The free model has no TTFA/DPA commitments or SLA, requests may be used to improve model quality, and its free window has had its end date extended several times.
Default concurrency is 5 requests until $100 has been prepaid; higher tiers unlock at $100 (15) and $1,000 (50).
The deprecated s1 model retires on December 31, 2026, and its emotion tags use a different syntax from S2.

stepsToMove: Create an API key in the Fish Audio console and send it as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'.
Native API: POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts with JSON including text, an optional reference_id (voice model id), format (mp3, wav, pcm or opus) and a 'model' header such as s2.1-pro.
To keep OpenAI SDK code, set base_url to https://api.fish.audio/compat/v1 and model to fish-audio/s2.1-pro; set response_format explicitly because the default is pcm.
To keep ElevenLabs SDK code, set the base URL to https://api.fish.audio/compat/elevenlabs and send the key via the xi-api-key header.
For streaming text input (LLM tokens) use the WebSocket TTS endpoint or the SDK stream_websocket helper; for text you already have use HTTP streaming.
Map voices: Fish uses its own voice IDs (reference_id), and cloned voices are created with the voice model API.

bestFor: Developers who want a large, expressive and multilingual voice catalogue with cloning and a free development model, and who are comfortable with per-byte pricing at about $15 per million characters for English.

Whether SSML is supported is not stated in the pages read; the vendor documents bracket tags and phoneme controls instead.
HIPAA, SOC 2 and GDPR compliance statements were not found.
The current end date of the s2.1-pro-free window is ambiguous because the blog lists several superseded dates; the latest stated is November 30, 2026.
Exact fair-use thresholds for s2.1-pro-free are not published on the pages read.
Latency figures differ between pages (about 70, 90, 100 and 300 ms) and are vendor-stated figures.
Web-app (Studio) subscription plan prices were not recorded because the pricing page is rendered client-side and the question concerns the API.
